title: A ROMAN EMPEROR?
sub: A Roman emperor's face, in gold, from the mud of Funan. But it isn't Roman.
say: A Roman emperor's face, in gold, from the mud of Foo-nahn. But it isn't Roman.

title: FUNAN
sub: Funan: a name from Chinese records for a Mekong Delta kingdom, roughly first to sixth or seventh century. Its own name is lost.
say: Foo-nahn: a name from Chinese records for a Mekong Delta kingdom, roughly first to sixth or seventh century. Its own name is lost.

title: THE WITNESSES
sub: Kang Tai and Zhu Ying, from the Chinese state of Wu, arrived around 245 to 250.
say: Kahng Tie and Joo Ying, from the Chinese state of Woo, arrived around two forty-five to two fifty.

title: WHAT THEY WROTE
sub: A later Chinese history says Funan had walled villages and palaces, and paid taxes in gold, pearls and perfume.
say: A later Chinese history says Foo-nahn had walled villages and palaces, and paid taxes in gold, pearls and perfume.

title: ONLY COPIES
sub: But their own reports are lost, surviving only as fragments in later histories.
say: But their own reports are lost, surviving only as fragments in later histories.

title: THE MUD
sub: In 1944, French archaeologist Louis Malleret dug at Óc Eo, in today's southern Vietnam.
say: In nineteen forty-four, French archaeologist Louis Mal-uh-ray dug at Ock Ay-oh, in today's southern Vietnam.

title: A PORT
sub: A port town, with moats, a canal toward the sea, and objects linked to India and China.
say: A port town, with moats, a canal toward the sea, and objects linked to India and China.

title: THE DISC
sub: And a thin gold disc copying an Antoninus Pius coin design from 152. Garbled letters, a broken loop: a pendant, not a coin.
say: And a thin gold disc copying an Antoh-nine-us Pie-us coin design from one fifty-two. Garbled letters, a broken loop: a pendant, not a coin.

title: THE ANSWER
sub: Roman coins reached India through trade. Where this copy was made, in India or in the delta itself, scholars aren't sure.
say: Roman coins reached India through trade. Where this copy was made, in India or in the delta itself, scholars aren't sure.

title: THE FADE
sub: Funan's name lasts in Chinese records into the six hundreds. They describe Chenla, to the north, absorbing its lands.
say: Foo-nahn's name lasts in Chinese records into the six hundreds. They describe Chen-lah, to the north, absorbing its lands.

title: ONE KINGDOM?
sub: But was Funan one kingdom? Historian Michael Vickery thought it more likely a group of ports, taking turns to lead.
say: But was Foo-nahn one kingdom? Historian Michael Vickery thought it more likely a group of ports, taking turns to lead.

title: TODAY
sub: Its sites lie in both Vietnam and Cambodia. In 2026, Vietnam nominated Óc Eo for World Heritage.
say: Its sites lie in both Vietnam and Cambodia. In twenty twenty-six, Vietnam nominated Ock Ay-oh for World Heritage.

title: RICE & EMPIRES
sub: And the disc? In 2006, the museum said it had been missing since 1975. An emperor's face reached the Mekong. The kingdom's own name never reached us.
say: And the disc? In two thousand six, the museum said it had been missing since nineteen seventy-five. An emperor's face reached the Mekong. The kingdom's own name never reached us.
